newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian officials summon ITC chief for questioning.
newsitem.headline: Indian officials summon ITC chief for questioning.

text.p: Indian enforcement directorate officials on Thursday summoned chairman of tobacco giant ITC Ltd, Yogesh Deveshwar, a day after a director and three former officials were arrested for alleged violations of foreign exchange norms.
"Deveshwar is being interrogated. His house has been searched in the morning," a senior directorate official who did not want to be named told Reuters in Calcutta.
The official said Deveshwar was taken in for questioning a short while after he arrived in Calcutta from New Delhi on Thursday.
The directorate official was unwilling to comment further on the interrogation but said Deveshwar, who took over as chairman in January, 1996, was still being questioned.
"We can give you more details in the evening," the official said.
The directorate had arrested R.K. Kutty, director-in-charge of the international business division of ITC, on Wednesday along with three former executives.
Saurav Misra, one of the deputy chairmen of the firm, and a former chairman J.N. Sapru were also summoned for interrogation and detained past midnight on Wednesday, the official said.
Another former chairman, K.L. Chugh, will be summoned for questioning on Friday, officials said.
More than a hundred directorate officials swooped on the homes of several former and present ITC officials in four cities on Wednesday.
ITC's headquarters in Calcutta were also searched and two of its floors have been sealed since Wedneday.
Officials also searched the office of its international business division.
Enforcement directorate said they have enough evidence to prove violation of India's foreign exchange rules made by ITC since 1991.
